record.question: Which among the following is true about Primary vs Secondary memory?
options: Primary memory is non-volatile, Secondary memory is volatile
Primary memory is faster but temporary, Secondary memory is slower but permanent
Secondary memory directly communicates with CPU
record.explanation: B is the uniquely best printed comparison in the conventional primary-working-memory-versus-secondary-storage sense. NIELIT's original O-Level RAM lesson explicitly calls RAM primary/main/system memory, identifies its volatile retention and states it is faster than secondary memory. A reverses the volatility relationship, C falsely makes secondary storage volatile, and D is not the standard primary/secondary distinction. The terminology is broader in some classifications, which include nonvolatile ROM under primary storage, so the solution must explicitly state that this comparison concerns ordinary working RAM and must explain permanent as retention without power, not indefinite preservation. Precision note: Here primary means ordinary working RAM, and permanent means nonvolatile retention. Broader primary-storage taxonomies may also include nonvolatile ROM; secondary storage is not guaranteed to retain data forever. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.nielit.gov.in/gorakhpur/sites/default/files/Gorakhpur/OLevel_2_ICT_20mar.pdf; https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/primary-vs-secondary-storage
